name: Flies
overview: The Scriptures reveal God's sovereign power over creation through the plague of flies sent upon Egypt as a judgment against Pharaoh's stubbornness, while sparing His own people in Goshen as a sign of His protective presence (Exodus 8:21-24). This divine intervention not only demonstrated God's authority to corrupt the land with swarms of flies but also established a clear separation between His people and the Egyptians, underscoring His redemptive purpose (Exodus 8:22-23). The narrative further highlights the tension between obedience to God and cultural compromise, as Moses refuses to offer sacrifices that would honor Egyptian idolatry, emphasizing faithfulness to the true God (Exodus 8:25-26).
